answer: Macrophages contribute to prenatal skin blood vessel formation through promoting angiogenesis and blood vessel morphogenesis. Different macrophage subsets play specific roles: LYVE1+ and TREM2+ microglia-like macrophages promote sprouting angiogenesis and blood vessel morphogenesis, while iron-recycling macrophages promote endothelial cell chemotaxis. Co-culture experiments demonstrated that macrophages are required for proper vascular network formation and remodeling.
support_quote: Gene module expression profiles suggested that sprouting angiogenesis (growth of new vessels) was promoted by LYVE1+ and TML macrophages, blood vessel morphogenesis by LYVE1+ macrophages and endothelial cell chemotaxis by iron-recycling macrophages
